key_insight: The paper introduces an open-source hardware-software toolkit that automates RHEED control and analysis so AI agents can guide thin-film growth in a more autonomous, quantitative way.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the barrier to integrating in situ diagnostics, programmable instrument control, and agentic workflows into thin-film synthesis platforms such as pulsed laser deposition systems.
method: Programmable electron-optics control with automated beam alignment and rocking-curve acquisition
Training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment plus shared GUI/programmatic analysis interfaces
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and extensible adapters for AI-driven analysis and RHEED simulation
evidence_signal: The toolkit was demonstrated on a pulsed laser deposition system, including an agent-driven natural-language workflow that selected, configured, and executed quantitative analyses.
watch_item: Autonomous performance will still depend on robust calibration, instrument-specific integration, and the reliability of newly added community methods.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
